19/Oct/26 11:55 PM;62850ed5bdf2f30067d3f477;*Status of ONLINE-7857 (2026-10-20)*

This ticket was split into two parts on 2026-10-16. The *cost* part is built and on dev. The *access and licensing* part has not been started.

*Built (cost)*

# *AI cost per Scout tool, measured* from the per-turn cost Scout already logs. These figures come from local development and test runs (1,637 turns, Oct 10–15), not real classroom use, so they show the cost of each action, not how much teachers will use it.

||Tool||Average cost per use||
|Lesson pack|$0.08|
|Single lesson plan|$0.08|
|Weekly plan|$0.09 (4 samples only)|
|Slides|$0.05|
|Question set|$0.04|
|Report cards|$0.03 (3 samples only)|
|Leveling|$0.015|
|District Insights question|$0.02|
|Quick question|$0.013|
|Class feedback|about $0.22 per run (test runs only)|

# *Weekly usage cap per teacher: $2.50 of AI cost per week* (the week starts Monday, UTC).
#* It is sized from a modelled medium-use teacher week of $2.22: 2 lesson packs, 2 slide decks, 1 weekly plan, 3 lesson plans, 4 levelings, 3 question sets, 3 report-card requests, 2 class-feedback runs, 10 page actions, 50 quick questions and 5 grading calls.
#* Over a 36-week school year this limits one seat to at most about $90 of AI cost; a medium year is about $80.
#* The cap counts AI cost, not messages, so a lesson pack uses more of it than a quick question.
#* When the cap is reached, Scout stops and says when the allowance resets, in the teacher's local time.
#* The existing $5 daily cap and per-user rate limits are unchanged.
#* This has not yet been checked against the seat price, which isn't recorded in the system.
# *Where it is:* on dev now (Scout service deployed 2026-10-19). For production, it ships with the release MRs (swo !6315, rag !99).

*Not built (access and licensing)*

These parts were deliberately left for later and were never started:

* Scout off until a district or school opts in, with the district setting overriding the teacher's.
* Seats granted to a district, which the district admin assigns and moves between teachers, including rostered teachers.
* A total of seats in use for the district admin.
* School-year licenses that expire on June 30.
* A 30-day district pilot.
* A "Contact us to add seats" message for teachers without a seat.

Today Scout access is still controlled by the existing feature flags. These items move to their own ticket, ONLINE-7874, so this ticket covers only the cost work.

*How QA can test the cap* (dev; the counter is reset on request):

# Use a teacher account until the week's AI cost passes $2.50, or ask Salman to set the account's counter near the cap.
# Ask Scout anything. It should refuse with a message giving the reset day and time in the teacher's local time.
# A message within the cap still works as before.

column3: [AI Project] Scout access and licensing: district opt-in, seats assigned by district admins, school-year licenses and pilots
column5:
Split out of ONLINE-7857 on 2026-10-20. ONLINE-7857 now covers only cost: the per-tool cost measurement and the weekly usage cap, both built. The access and licensing items below have not been started. Today Scout access is still controlled by the existing feature flags.

h2. Access

* *Off by default.* Scout is off until a district (or school) opts in. A district's setting always overrides a teacher's, including a seat the teacher holds.
* *Seats assigned by district admins.* The district is granted a number of seats. The district admin picks which teachers get Scout and can move a seat to another teacher. This works for rostered users.
* *Seat totals.* The district admin sees every active seat in the district, however it was granted.
* *School-year licenses.* Seats reset on June 30 and must be renewed, with no pro-rating.
* *Pilot.* Turn Scout on for every teacher in a district for 30 days, then keep it only for the teachers given seats.
* When a teacher without a seat opens Scout, show a "Contact us to add seats" message.
* The system only knows which seats were granted; prices and discounts stay in the quote tool.

h2. Later

* Teacher self-purchase in SWO (see ONLINE-5621).
* Shout-outs for top Scout users.

h2. Related

* ONLINE-7857 (cost and weekly cap), ONLINE-7489 (prod monitoring and cost control), ONLINE-5621 (payment for AI tools).

h2. Done when

* A district with Scout off shows no Scout to any teacher.
* A district admin can grant, move and count seats.
* Seats expire on June 30.
* A pilot turns on, and ends on its date.
